label_review.notes: Proposed labels follow the authored pair intent. A human reviewer must inspect every rendered pair and sign off before live measurements.

fire.title: Heading clipped at the viewport edge

clean.title: Long heading wraps intentionally

fire.title: Audit label chopped inside a fixed cell

fire.adjudication_notes: The label is visibly chopped inside an overflow-hidden cell and cannot be recovered from adjacent content.

clean.title: Dense expert table scrolls without truncating labels
clean.truth_excerpt: Dense expert surfaces are allowed when their labels remain available.
clean.adjudication_notes: The table is intentionally dense, but the label is complete and the horizontal overflow affordance is visible.

fire.title: Three primary treatments compete

fire.adjudication_notes: A huge title, saturated diagram, and equally large KPI row all demand first attention, leaving no single focal point.

clean.title: Dense evidence supports one dominant diagram
clean.truth_excerpt: The router is the claim; supporting metrics may remain subordinate.
clean.adjudication_notes: The surface contains many expert details, but scale and contrast clearly make the router diagram the single focal element.

fire.title: Every dashboard tile is visually primary
fire.truth_excerpt: The decision is whether recall remains above the graduation gate.
fire.adjudication_notes: Four equally loud metric tiles and two charts compete despite one decision-driving measure.

clean.title: Expert dashboard emphasizes the decision metric
clean.truth_excerpt: Recall is the decision-driving measure; other metrics are supporting context.
clean.adjudication_notes: The dashboard remains information-dense but recall is clearly dominant through placement and type scale.

fire.title: Tiny diagram floats in unexplained space
fire.truth_excerpt: The three-stage route is the full content of the slide.
fire.adjudication_notes: The diagram occupies a small corner while most of the canvas is unexplained blank space, making the content feel missing.

clean.title: Authored breathing room frames a short claim
clean.truth_excerpt: The brief calls for a quiet transition slide with one compact route.
clean.adjudication_notes: The blank area is deliberately balanced around a centered claim and does not resemble a collapsed or missing region.

fire.title: Collapsed third column leaves accidental dead space
fire.truth_excerpt: All three peer stages have content in the source brief.
fire.adjudication_notes: The third stage collapses to a tiny block and leaves a large blank region that reads as missing content.

clean.title: Evidence rail intentionally leaves reading space
clean.truth_excerpt: The composition is an editorial 70/30 narrative and evidence split.
clean.adjudication_notes: The narrow evidence rail and open lower area are authored hierarchy, not a missing peer column.

fire.title: Equivalent peer tracks drift in width
fire.truth_excerpt: The three stages are declared as equivalent review tracks.
fire.adjudication_notes: The middle track is inexplicably narrower and divider positions do not align across otherwise equivalent regions.

clean.title: Intentional 60/40 editorial split
clean.truth_excerpt: The narrative is primary and the evidence rail is explicitly supporting.
clean.adjudication_notes: The unequal widths express different content roles and therefore should not be treated as failed peer symmetry.

fire.title: Peer row baselines do not align
fire.truth_excerpt: Rows represent direct before/after counterparts.
fire.adjudication_notes: Corresponding row dividers drift vertically, undermining the declared one-to-one comparison.

clean.title: Content-driven masonry is not a peer table
clean.truth_excerpt: Items are independent editorial fragments with deliberately varied lengths.
clean.adjudication_notes: The staggered baselines belong to an editorial masonry composition, not equivalent repeated rows.

fire.title: One peer quadrant appears absent
fire.truth_excerpt: The operating loop defines four peer responsibilities.
fire.adjudication_notes: One quadrant receives a fraction of the area and large accidental whitespace makes it appear unimplemented.

clean.title: One dominant result spans two grid columns
clean.truth_excerpt: The result is explicitly the conclusion and should dominate supporting inputs.
clean.adjudication_notes: The spanning result is intentional hierarchy rather than an equivalent peer rendered at the wrong size.

fire.title: Controls crowd the primary claim
fire.truth_excerpt: The page title and selected policy are the primary content.
fire.adjudication_notes: Large controls surround and visually overpower the title, producing several competing focal targets.

clean.title: Compact expert controls remain subordinate
clean.truth_excerpt: Frequent operators need all controls available without losing the page claim.
clean.adjudication_notes: The surface is dense by design, but compact chrome remains subordinate to one clear title and active policy.

fire.title: Swimlanes and containment conflict
fire.truth_excerpt: The content describes one request flow.
fire.adjudication_notes: Half the figure uses lanes while the other half uses nested containment for the same relation.

clean.title: One flow grammar with a highlighted boundary
clean.truth_excerpt: The boundary denotes deployment ownership inside one request flow.
clean.adjudication_notes: A boundary annotation does not create a second diagram type; connectors and nodes retain one stable grammar.

fire.title: One-day and six-month gaps look equal
fire.truth_excerpt: The milestones occur after one day and then roughly six months.
fire.adjudication_notes: Equal visual spacing materially misrepresents the stated time intervals.

clean.title: Compressed timeline explicitly marks a break
clean.truth_excerpt: The timeline is compressed and must disclose the discontinuity.
clean.adjudication_notes: A visible axis break and label make the non-linear spacing explicit rather than deceptively proportional.

fire.title: Near-equal bars represent a fourfold difference
fire.truth_excerpt: The second value is four times the first.
fire.adjudication_notes: The bars differ only slightly in length, visually erasing a load-bearing fourfold ratio.

clean.title: Symbolic comparison avoids a false quantitative scale
clean.truth_excerpt: The composition is a labeled comparison and does not claim scaled bar length.
clean.adjudication_notes: Equal containers are acceptable because explicit values carry the comparison and no quantitative axis is implied.

fire.title: Legend names an absent cache category
fire.truth_excerpt: Only API and Store categories are drawn.
fire.adjudication_notes: The legend includes Cache even though no corresponding mark exists in the figure.

clean.title: Muted category still appears in the figure
clean.truth_excerpt: Cache is present but intentionally de-emphasized because it is inactive.
clean.adjudication_notes: Every legend category has a plotted counterpart; low emphasis is not absence.

fire.title: Decision nodes lack a legend entry
fire.truth_excerpt: Diamonds encode decisions and rectangles encode services.
fire.adjudication_notes: A distinct load-bearing diamond category is used repeatedly but the legend never defines it.

clean.title: Annotation callout does not need a legend category
clean.truth_excerpt: The lone dashed note is explanatory annotation, not a data category.
clean.adjudication_notes: A conventional one-off annotation is self-labelled and does not create an unexplained visual category.

fire.title: Three independent bullets are boxed and arrowed
fire.truth_excerpt: The brief lists three independent qualities with no sequence or relationship.
fire.adjudication_notes: Boxes and arrows add a false flow while conveying no information beyond a short list.

clean.title: Three nodes expose a real dependency
clean.truth_excerpt: Graduation requires adjudication, which requires captured observations.
clean.adjudication_notes: The connectors encode necessary dependency and therefore add information beyond the labels.

fire.title: Model comparison is an arbitrary node graph
fire.truth_excerpt: The source contains aligned latency, accuracy, and cost values.
fire.adjudication_notes: A graph obscures exact aligned comparisons that a compact table would communicate more faithfully.

clean.title: Network topology needs relational placement
clean.truth_excerpt: The claim depends on fan-out, shared stores, and retry paths.
clean.adjudication_notes: Topology and connector direction are load-bearing; a flat table would discard the relevant relationships.

fire.title: Two unrelated nodes claim equal dominance
fire.truth_excerpt: The narrative job is to explain policy routing.
fire.adjudication_notes: Two saturated oversized nodes compete even though only the router is load-bearing to the claim.

clean.title: Two endpoints frame one dominant transformation
clean.truth_excerpt: The policy router is the transformation under explanation.
clean.adjudication_notes: Endpoints remain visible but the central router is unmistakably dominant.

fire.title: Hierarchy and sequence use identical connectors
fire.truth_excerpt: The source distinguishes reporting hierarchy from workflow sequence.
fire.adjudication_notes: Identical lines and boxes collapse two different relation types into an incoherent grammar.

clean.title: Uniform node forest is the requested inventory
clean.visible_text: Service A · Service B · Service C
clean.truth_excerpt: The figure is an inventory grouped only by deployment zone.
clean.adjudication_notes: Uniform boxes are truthful because the nodes are genuine peers and containment is the sole relation.

fire.title: Named outcomes consume more than the whole
fire.truth_excerpt: Displayed probabilities must sum to the complete distribution.
fire.adjudication_notes: The visual encodes 110 percent while presenting a complete distribution, a material proportional contradiction.

clean.title: Residual probability remains visible
clean.truth_excerpt: Residual probability is material and must remain represented.
clean.adjudication_notes: All proportions sum to one hundred percent and the residual category is explicitly preserved.

fire.title: Two control planes receive equal visual dominance
fire.visible_text: Admission Gate · Policy Engine · Audit Store
fire.truth_excerpt: The policy engine is the decision-making center; admission and audit are supporting boundaries.
fire.adjudication_notes: The admission gate and policy engine are both oversized and saturated, so the diagram gives two competing answers to what controls the system.

clean.title: One policy engine dominates supporting boundaries
clean.visible_text: Admission Gate · Policy Engine · Audit Store
clean.truth_excerpt: The policy engine is the decision-making center; admission and audit are supporting boundaries.
clean.adjudication_notes: The central policy engine receives the sole dominant treatment while the admission gate and audit store remain legible supporting endpoints.

fire.title: Hard-coded dark panel leaks into light mode
fire.truth_excerpt: Both screenshots should express the same preset in their respective mode.
fire.adjudication_notes: One panel remains dark only in the light screenshot and its text fails to invert with the rest of the preset.

clean.title: Dark data surface is intentional in both modes
clean.truth_excerpt: The embedded terminal is explicitly a dark simulated surface in either page mode.
clean.adjudication_notes: The stable dark terminal is content semantics, not a failed page-mode inversion, and its own text remains readable.

fire.title: Icons disappear against the dark surface
fire.truth_excerpt: Icon and label meaning must remain visible in both modes.
fire.adjudication_notes: The dark screenshot retains a dark icon fill, making load-bearing symbols effectively invisible.

clean.title: Decorative watermark fades in dark mode
clean.truth_excerpt: The watermark is non-semantic decoration and may be quiet.
clean.adjudication_notes: All load-bearing icons and text remain visible; only a deliberately non-semantic watermark loses prominence.

fire.title: Orange tints an entire status section
fire.truth_excerpt: Mono-Industrial reserves color for specific values with status meaning.
fire.adjudication_notes: Orange colors a container and heading without representing an actual warning value.

clean.title: One warning value carries orange
clean.truth_excerpt: Three delayed items are a measured warning state.
clean.adjudication_notes: Color is scoped to the precise delayed count and therefore conveys genuine value semantics.

fire.title: Several unrelated elements break the grid
fire.truth_excerpt: The preset permits one deliberate compositional or typographic surprise.
fire.adjudication_notes: Three rotated and oversized elements break the system, so no single authored surprise remains.

clean.title: One oversized decision breaks the pattern
clean.truth_excerpt: The decision is the one intended moment of surprise.
clean.adjudication_notes: Exactly one typographic element breaks the otherwise consistent system and the break supports hierarchy.

fire.title: Five equally loud emphasis layers
fire.truth_excerpt: The active preset calls for three legible emphasis layers.
fire.adjudication_notes: Multiple near-equal weights and sizes create at least five competing emphasis levels with no stable hierarchy.

clean.title: Dense page resolves into three emphasis layers
clean.truth_excerpt: Dense content is compatible with three clearly grouped emphasis levels.
clean.adjudication_notes: Many elements are present, but they resolve into a dominant hero, section level, and quiet instrument text.

fire.title: Red accent is a decorative underline
fire.truth_excerpt: Nothing red is reserved for urgent, destructive, or error meaning.
fire.adjudication_notes: The single red use merely decorates a neutral heading and communicates no status.

clean.title: Red marks a destructive reset action
clean.truth_excerpt: Resetting the policy is destructive and requires explicit warning.
clean.adjudication_notes: The red accent is scoped to a genuine destructive action rather than used as ornament.

fire.title: Three cards independently escape the grid
fire.truth_excerpt: The preset allows one meaningful grid break.
fire.adjudication_notes: Several arbitrary offsets break the composition without establishing one deliberate exception.

clean.title: Full-width navigation is ordinary chrome
clean.truth_excerpt: Full-width navigation is excluded from the single content-grid-break count.
clean.adjudication_notes: One content element breaks the grid; the full-width navigation is legitimate chrome and not a second break.

fire.title: Glossy rounded demo conflicts with flat host
fire.truth_excerpt: The host preset uses flat square surfaces and restrained borders.
fire.adjudication_notes: Large radius, glow, and heavy shadow make the demo feel pasted onto a visibly different design system.

clean.title: Functional browser chrome remains distinct
clean.truth_excerpt: The demo needs a minimal frame to communicate that it is interactive.
clean.adjudication_notes: The frame is functionally necessary and still matches the host’s radius, border, color, and caption treatment.

fire.title: Hero collapses into a tiny card on mobile
fire.truth_excerpt: The hero should remain intact and full-width on mobile.
fire.adjudication_notes: The primary claim is shrunk into one small bordered card among peers, destroying the intended hierarchy.

clean.title: Full-width mobile hero with compact supporting cards
clean.truth_excerpt: Supporting items may compact as long as the hero stays intact.
clean.adjudication_notes: The hero remains full-width and dominant while subordinate evidence becomes a denser mobile row.

fire.title: Dark mode keeps a light page background
fire.truth_excerpt: The named preset supports both light and dark surfaces.
fire.adjudication_notes: The dark-mode screenshot preserves the light canvas while inverting text, causing broken contrast and wrong-mode bleed.

clean.title: Paper inset remains light in both modes
clean.truth_excerpt: A print-preview inset intentionally represents white paper in either application mode.
clean.adjudication_notes: The light inset is an explicitly labelled paper preview with readable local colors, not a failed global inversion.

fire.title: Neutral queue total receives warning color
fire.truth_excerpt: A total case count is neutral unless a measured threshold has been exceeded.
fire.adjudication_notes: The colored status treatment decorates a neutral inventory count and implies a warning that the underlying value does not support.

clean.title: Threshold breach receives scoped warning color
clean.truth_excerpt: Twelve overdue cases exceed the documented queue threshold.
clean.adjudication_notes: The warning color is scoped to a measured threshold breach and therefore carries explicit status meaning rather than decoration.

fire.title: Multiple summary metrics independently break the grid
fire.truth_excerpt: Only the escalation decision is intended to break the otherwise regular summary grid.
fire.adjudication_notes: Several rotated and enlarged metrics compete as independent exceptions, leaving no single meaningful compositional surprise.

clean.title: One escalation decision breaks the summary grid
clean.truth_excerpt: Only the escalation decision is intended to break the otherwise regular summary grid.
clean.adjudication_notes: A single decision treatment departs from the regular grid while the supporting cost and recall measures retain the base system.

fire.title: Red badge decorates a neutral policy version
fire.truth_excerpt: The policy version is informational and has no urgent, destructive, or error state.
fire.adjudication_notes: Red is applied to a neutral version badge only for visual interest, creating false urgency without corresponding semantics.

clean.title: Red identifies irreversible policy deletion
clean.truth_excerpt: Deleting the policy version is irreversible and requires destructive emphasis.
clean.adjudication_notes: Red is limited to an irreversible deletion action, so the accent communicates the precise destructive meaning reserved by the preset.

fire.title: Several evidence cards use unrelated offsets
fire.truth_excerpt: The decision ledger is the sole content element intended to cross the grid.
fire.adjudication_notes: Multiple cards rotate and offset independently, turning the permitted single grid break into a collection of arbitrary exceptions.

clean.title: One decision ledger crosses the evidence grid
clean.truth_excerpt: The decision ledger is the sole content element intended to cross the grid.
clean.adjudication_notes: Only the decision ledger departs from the content grid; the surrounding source cards and ordinary chrome remain aligned.

fire.title: Soft gradient inspector conflicts with industrial host
fire.truth_excerpt: The host uses square panels, flat fills, and instrument-like typography.
fire.adjudication_notes: The embedded inspector introduces pill controls, gradients, glow, and soft shadows that visibly belong to a different design language.

clean.title: Inspector inherits the host surface language
clean.truth_excerpt: The inspector may retain functional controls while matching the host surface language.
clean.adjudication_notes: The embedded inspector retains necessary controls but matches the host’s square geometry, flat color, border weight, and typography.

fire.title: Four cards hide the selection policy
fire.truth_excerpt: A policy router assigns cases to distinct review queues with different entry rules.
fire.adjudication_notes: Equal cards name destinations but omit the router, mandatory path, sampling rule, and deduplication.

clean.title: Router exposes queue selection and overlap handling
clean.truth_excerpt: A policy router assigns cases to distinct review queues with different entry rules.
clean.adjudication_notes: The composition shows the universal gate, routing rules, separate queues, and deduplication path.

fire.title: Feedback loop is drawn as a one-way pipeline
fire.truth_excerpt: Deployment outcomes feed the next calibration cycle.
fire.adjudication_notes: The one-way pipeline omits the load-bearing return path and misstates the process as terminal.

clean.title: Feedback path returns outcomes to calibration
clean.truth_excerpt: Deployment outcomes feed the next calibration cycle.
clean.adjudication_notes: The return connector and its label make the iterative causal structure reconstructable.

fire.title: Named diagnoses omit residual uncertainty
fire.truth_excerpt: Fifteen percent residual probability remains material to the decision.
fire.adjudication_notes: The state looks complete while hiding residual uncertainty that changes downstream review behavior.

clean.title: Residual uncertainty remains an explicit branch
clean.truth_excerpt: Fifteen percent residual probability remains material to the decision.
clean.adjudication_notes: The full distribution and uncertain branch remain visible and connected to escalation.

fire.title: Evidence cards omit source-to-decision paths
fire.truth_excerpt: The viewer must reconstruct which source supports each decision claim.
fire.adjudication_notes: Grouped cards contain the right nouns but no connectors or identifiers preserve provenance.

clean.title: Trace IDs connect sources through findings to decisions
clean.truth_excerpt: The viewer must reconstruct which source supports each decision claim.
clean.adjudication_notes: Stable identifiers and connectors preserve the evidence path without requiring presenter narration.

fire.title: Resource allocation is shown as independent metrics
fire.truth_excerpt: Reviewer capacity governs queue throughput and the resulting SLA.
fire.adjudication_notes: Independent metrics conceal the load-bearing resource-to-throughput relationship.

clean.title: Capacity and queue connect to throughput and SLA
clean.truth_excerpt: Reviewer capacity governs queue throughput and the resulting SLA.
clean.adjudication_notes: The visual grammar exposes the governing flow and labels each transformation.

fire.title: Statuses appear without allowed transitions

fire.adjudication_notes: Status badges expose no transition rules and cannot communicate the allowed state changes.

clean.title: State machine exposes guarded transitions
clean.truth_excerpt: Cases can escalate from pending or reviewed, but only reviewed cases can close.
clean.adjudication_notes: Directed and labelled transitions make the guarded state changes reconstructable.

fire.title: Simple cost comparison becomes an elaborate system map
fire.truth_excerpt: The claim is a two-term break-even comparison.
fire.adjudication_notes: A complex network invents dependencies and obscures a claim that only needs aligned arithmetic.

clean.title: Aligned equation is proportionate to the claim
clean.truth_excerpt: The claim is a two-term break-even comparison.
clean.adjudication_notes: The relational treatment exposes the exact comparison without forcing an operating-model diagram.

fire.title: Cover claim is forced into a node graph
fire.truth_excerpt: The unit is a cover with one claim and no relational narrative job.
fire.adjudication_notes: A decorative graph implies a system the cover does not claim and is disproportionate to the unit.

clean.title: Cover remains a single dominant claim
clean.truth_excerpt: The unit is a cover with one claim and no relational narrative job.
clean.adjudication_notes: Routing to none is correct; no diagram is required for a single introductory claim.

fire.title: Interactive workflow is flattened into generic cards
fire.truth_excerpt: The clinician’s interaction among evidence, hypotheses, and actions is the claim.
fire.adjudication_notes: Three generic cards omit selection, comparison, and action state that define the workflow.

clean.title: Simulated workspace exposes the interaction
clean.truth_excerpt: The clinician’s interaction among evidence, hypotheses, and actions is the claim.
clean.adjudication_notes: The simulated surface faithfully exposes selection state, linked evidence, and available next actions.

fire.title: Dependency order is presented as unordered bullets
fire.truth_excerpt: Deployment requires schema before migration, then service, then client.
fire.adjudication_notes: An unordered list hides the load-bearing prerequisites and deploy order.

clean.title: Dependency map preserves prerequisites
clean.truth_excerpt: Deployment requires schema before migration, then service, then client.
clean.adjudication_notes: The ordered connectors expose every prerequisite and the final client dependency.

fire.title: Independent options are numbered and arrowed
fire.truth_excerpt: Users may choose Explore, Compare, or Export in any order.
fire.adjudication_notes: Numbers and arrows imply a required progression that the source explicitly does not establish.

clean.title: Numbered workflow follows real dependencies
clean.truth_excerpt: Adjudication requires captured observations; graduation requires adjudication.
clean.adjudication_notes: Every number and connector corresponds to a documented dependency and real order.

fire.title: Random section number implies missing chapters
fire.truth_excerpt: The artifact has one standalone page and no ordered sections.
fire.adjudication_notes: The isolated 04 marker implies a larger ordered document that does not exist.

clean.title: Section number resolves through the document agenda
clean.truth_excerpt: The agenda links Architecture as section four of six.

fire.title: Static mockup claims 87 percent confidence

clean.adjudication_notes: The measured value and its derivation are both visible, so the state implication is supported.

fire.title: Green dot claims a live connection
fire.truth_excerpt: The artifact is a static exported explainer with no connection telemetry.
fire.adjudication_notes: The conventional green status dot and “live” label imply a measured connection that cannot exist.

clean.title: Decorative dot is visibly non-status
clean.truth_excerpt: The dot is a typographic bullet before a neutral heading.

fire.title: Decorative progress bar implies task completion
fire.truth_excerpt: The page performs no analysis and tracks no progress.

clean.title: Deck progress reflects actual navigation

clean.adjudication_notes: The progress treatment is directly bound to real navigation state and accurately calculated.

fire.title: Citation marker has no source target
fire.truth_excerpt: The artifact supplies no source list, footnote, or link target.
fire.adjudication_notes: The bracketed marker conventionally implies traceable evidence that the artifact cannot provide.

clean.title: Footnote marker resolves to a supplied source

clean.adjudication_notes: The provenance cue is backed by a concrete source target in the artifact.

fire.title: Validated badge has no validation process
fire.truth_excerpt: No validator, review event, or source record exists.
fire.adjudication_notes: The checkmark and validation label assert provenance and verification unsupported by the artifact.

clean.title: Validation badge links to a signed review event
clean.truth_excerpt: Review event R-184 names the reviewer, timestamp, and checked sources.
clean.adjudication_notes: The validation claim resolves to a real review record with traceable provenance.

fire.title: Decorative source strip invents freshness
fire.truth_excerpt: The content is static prose with no source feed or retrieval time.
fire.adjudication_notes: Source and timestamp chrome imply a live traceable feed that the artifact does not possess.

clean.title: Snapshot timestamp identifies a real retrieval
clean.truth_excerpt: Dataset version 18 was retrieved at 12:42 UTC and is bundled with the report.
clean.adjudication_notes: The timestamp and version accurately identify a supplied snapshot rather than manufacturing freshness.

fire.title: Fake terminal reports successful deployment
fire.truth_excerpt: The artifact never ran a deployment command and has no execution result.
fire.adjudication_notes: Terminal chrome and SUCCESS output imply an executed command and measured state that never occurred.

fire.title: Parallel choices are connected as a pipeline

clean.title: Branching connector shows mutually exclusive choices
